![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14223941/assets/ffdfbbfcbc2a01e79fd9490f05744b2d0bf1d24dd616a0b318ee95acfa26e9ba.png)

A cone-shaped pile of salt is being depleted so that the volume of the pile decreases at $5\pi \,{\text{m}}^{3}/\text{hr}.$ The height of the pile is always one-half of its base diameter. Find the rate of the pile’s height decrease when the height is $5\,\text{m}.$ Do not round the answer.

*Hint*: Assume that the rate of decrease is positive.

The height is decreasing at a rate of
{{field-1}} $\text{m}/\text{hr}.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's call $h$ the height of the pile and $r$ the radius of its base. Both of these quantities, as well as the volume $v,$ change with time. In particular, we know that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=-5\pi \,{\text{m}}^{3}/\text{hr},
$$

and we want to find $\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}$ when $h=5\,\text{m}.$

We need to find a relation between $h$ and the variable for which we know the rate of change, which is $v.$ This is given by the formula for the volume of a cone:

$$
v=\frac{1}{3}\pi {r}^{2}h
$$

Before we differentiate the equation with respect to time, note that $r$ also appears in the formula. So, we need to simplify the formula by writing $r$ in terms of $h.$

We're told that the height is always one-half of its base diameter. So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}h & =\frac{1}{2}d \\ h & =\frac{1}{2}(2r) \\ r & =h.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the volume formula as

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{1}{3}\pi {r}^{2}h \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\pi (h)^{2}h \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\pi {h}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now that we have an equation relating $v$ and $h,$ we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}v & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{3}\pi {h}^{3}) \\  & =\pi {h}^{2}\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting the known values and solving for $\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-5\pi  & =\pi (5)^{2}\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} \\ -5\pi  & =25\pi \frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} & =-\frac{1}{5}\,\text{m}/\text{hr}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the height of the pile is decreasing at a rate of $\frac{1}{5}\,\text{m}/\text{hr}.$
